newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Albright says good start to talks in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Albright says good start to talks in Moscow.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Thursday she had made a good start to talks with Russian leaders in Moscow.

"I think we had some good meetings. It was a matter of establishing a relationship and getting to know each other," she told reporters after talks with Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"Then we got down to work," she said.
Albright, who is on her first trip to Russia as secretary of state, declined to give details of her discussions on NATO's plans to expand eastwards, which are opposed by Moscow.
"I am not going to characterise those at this point," she said.

Asked if she had come to Moscow to check on President Boris Yeltsin's health following a bout of pneumonia, she said she had come to discuss plans for a planned summit in Helsinki next month between Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Her spokesman, Nicholas Burns, said the meetings had been "very constructuve and very detailed" and conducted in a warm atmosphere.
He quoted Primakov as telling Albright: "I'm going to be nice to you".

Burns said topics had included a "range of issues" which each sides felt should be discussed in Helsinki and proposals NATO is making to try to ease Russian fears over the Western alliance's plans to offer membership to former Warsaw Pact states.
